Consult Summary:
- Patient reports six-week history of unilateral left ear hearing loss with intermittent left-ear tinnitus and mild dizziness; plan to obtain an in-person ear examination to exclude wax blockage and assess for other causes, with tinnitus education provided and clinic booking arranged within 4–5 days.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Six-week history of left-ear hearing loss with intermittent tinnitus and mild dizziness.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began about six weeks ago; fluctuating/on-and-off with triggers noted.
- Symptom progression: Persistent left-ear hearing difficulty with intermittent tinnitus; dizziness described as off-balance rather than spinning.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Tinnitus loudness can be modulated by sound exposure (watching TV or listening to music may reduce the ringing).
- Associated symptoms: No left-ear pain; no ear discharge; no fever; dizziness without nausea or vertigo described; no itching noted.
- Laterality: Hearing loss primarily in the left ear; right ear sensations normal.
- Relevant past events: Prior transient hearing issue about a year ago lasting a couple of days (not described as ongoing).
- Systems review: Positive for tinnitus in the left ear and intermittent dizziness; no chest pain, palpitations, fever, or ear discharge reported.
- Plan-related notes from conversation: Ear evaluation to exclude wax impaction or other blockage; consideration of other etiologies after exam; tinnitus education planned.

Past Medical History:
- Prior transient hearing problem about 1 year ago (details not provided).
- No other PMH documented.
- Allergies: None documented.
- Medications: None documented.

Social History:
- Not documented.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- vitals: Not provided.
- examination findings: Not documented (planning to perform otoscopic ear examination).

Investigations:
- Otoscopic/ear examination to be performed by GP within 4–5 days to assess for wax impaction or other pathology.
- If wax blockage identified, wax removal indicated.
- If no blockage found, consider other etiologies of unilateral hearing loss and tinnitus.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Unilateral (left) hearing loss with tinnitus and intermittent dizziness.
  - Plan:
    - Schedule face-to-face ear examination with a GP within 4–5 days to inspect ear canal and tympanic membrane.
    - If blockage (wax) is present, perform wax removal.
    - If no blockage, pursue further assessment for other causes of unilateral hearing loss and tinnitus.
    - Provide patient education about tinnitus; link to leaflet to read prior to or after the appointment.
    - Clinic follow-up: the upcoming appointment will be with a GP who will review notes and conduct the ear check.
- Issue 2: Dizziness/off-balance sensation in the context of ear symptoms.
  - Plan:
    - Evaluate during the ear exam; if persistent or concerning features emerge, plan further evaluation as indicated.
- Issue 3: General management and follow-up logistics.
  - Plan:
    - Provide tinnitus educational resources (link to leaflet).
    - Facilitate appointment scheduling with a GP; notes from this consult will be available to the clinician.
    - If any issues arise before the scheduled clinic appointment, consider a brief video consult.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies not documented.
  - Current medications not documented.
  - Comprehensive past medical history not documented beyond a single prior ear issue.
  - Social history (smoking, alcohol, substance use) not documented.
  - Family history not documented.
  - Vital signs and formal physical exam findings not documented.
- Internal conflicts: None detected; no conflicting statements in the transcript.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some topics (e.g., full PMH, social history) were not elaborated in the conversation. No major inaudible segments.
